plain: The public JSON document a UCP business serves at /.well-known/ucp. It lists the protocol version, services and transports, capabilities, payment handlers and the business's public signing keys.
ste: The JSON document at /.well-known/ucp. It shows the versions, transports, capabilities, payment handlers and public keys of a business.

plain: The profile a UCP platform publishes at a URL of its choice and names in the UCP-Agent header; it lists the platform's capabilities, keys and settings such as an order webhook URL.
ste: The JSON document of the platform. The platform sends its address in the UCP-Agent header.

plain: The HTTP request header in which a UCP platform names its profile URL, in RFC 8941 dictionary syntax (profile="..."). Over MCP the same value goes in meta ucp-agent.
ste: An HTTP header. It contains the address of the platform profile.

plain: The UCP negotiation step in which the business keeps only capabilities both profiles list, picks the highest version both support, and prunes extensions whose parent capability is gone.
ste: The set of capabilities that the business and the platform both support, at the highest common version.

plain: The UCP rule that a capability's schema URL host must match its reverse-DNS name. It proves who published a schema, not that the publisher is trustworthy.
ste: A rule. The host of the schema address must agree with the name of the capability.

plain: In UCP, a specification written by a credential provider (for example com.google.pay) that a business configures and a platform executes to obtain an opaque payment token.
ste: A specification from a credential provider. The platform uses it to get a payment token.

plain: A trusted party, such as a digital wallet, that manages a user's payment and identity credentials and issues tokens to a platform.
ste: A wallet or similar party that keeps the payment credentials of the buyer and gives tokens.

plain: An absolute HTTPS URL a business returns so the buyer can finish a checkout on the business's own interface; required in UCP when status is requires_escalation.
ste: The address of the web checkout of the business. The buyer uses it to finish the order.

plain: In UCP, the checkout status that hands the purchase from the agent to the buyer because the business needs input its API cannot collect or a policy needs the buyer to review the order.
ste: A checkout status. The agent must give the checkout to the buyer through the continue_url.

plain: The UCP capability that links a buyer's account at a business to a platform with OAuth 2.0 authorization code and PKCE S256, using scopes derived from capabilities.
ste: A capability that connects the account of the buyer at a business to the platform with OAuth 2.0.

plain: A UCP checkout session in which the AP2 extension was negotiated, so the business must sign every checkout and neither side may fall back to an unprotected checkout.
ste: A session that uses AP2 mandates. The session cannot change back to a checkout without mandates.

plain: The business's detached JWS signature over a JCS-canonical UCP checkout, sent in every checkout response when the AP2 extension is active.
ste: The signature of the business on the checkout. The platform must verify it before it shows the checkout.

plain: A UCP service entry that pairs a transport (rest, mcp, a2a or embedded) with an endpoint and a machine-readable description such as OpenAPI or OpenRPC.
ste: An entry in the profile. It connects a transport to an endpoint.

plain: The UCP resource a platform creates and updates until it can be completed; it has an id, line items, totals, required legal links, a status and an expiry.
ste: The checkout resource. The platform makes it, changes it and completes it.
